body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students order three objects by length and compare two lengths indirectly by using a third object (1.MD.A.1).
- Students measure length as a whole number of same-size units laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps (1.MD.A.2).
- Students tell and write time in hours and half hours on analog and digital clocks (1.MD.B.3).
- Students organize, represent and interpret data with up to three categories, and answer how many in all and how many more (1.MD.C.4).

MATERIALS
- Connecting cubes, paper clips (all the same size) and string
- Classroom objects of different lengths to measure: pencils, books, shoes, ribbons
- A geared demonstration clock and a paper-plate clock for each student
- A class chart with three columns, sticky notes or tally marks
- Tablets with the class activities open, for photos of work

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read How Long? What Time? together. Line up three students by height, then compare two classroom objects that cannot be put side by side using a string. Lesson activity: How Long Is It?
Day 2: Measure and Compare. Measure objects with cubes in pairs. Show what happens when cubes have gaps or overlap (the number changes). Students complete the assignment.
Day 3: Clocks. Show the hour hand alone moving from 3 to 4. Then show 3:30, with the hour hand halfway. Students make times on paper-plate clocks and begin Clocks and Charts.
Day 4: Data. Take a class vote with three choices and record it as a chart. Ask: which got the most? how many more? how many in all? Students finish Clocks and Charts.
Day 5: Assessment: Measuring and Time Check. Read each problem aloud. Students may use cubes and clocks.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: give measuring strips with a start line. Measure only with cubes before paper clips. Use an hour-hand-only clock for hours before adding the minute hand.
- Support: for "how many more", line up the two groups of sticky notes and count the extras.
- Stretch: measure the same object with cubes and with paper clips and explain why the numbers differ; tell the time one hour later and one half hour later.
- Multilingual learners: teach longer, shorter, longest, shortest, hour, half past and o'clock with objects and the clock. Both "4:30" and "half past four" are correct; teach both.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
We are measuring, telling time and reading charts. At home, measure things with spoons or paper clips: how many spoons long is the table? Point out the clock at bedtime or dinnertime and ask your child what time it is, to the hour or half hour (7:00 or 7:30). You can also take a family vote, such as a favorite fruit, and count the votes together.
title: Teacher guide: Measuring and Telling Time
